collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — ADVICE AND DECISIONS (ADV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Asking for advice, giving it, ignoring it, following half of it, and deciding alone. Advice can be wrong, even from elders and experts. Following it doesn't guarantee a good outcome and ignoring it doesn't cause a bad one. Feeling heard with no decision is a perfectly good ending, and nobody ever has to admit someone else was right.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an elder who builds and a young adult)

collection.description: An elder builder admits their roof-lashing advice was wrong: thank them, or ask why.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Last season, (subject), the most experienced builder on Isola, told (friend) to always lash the roof poles with three turns of rope. Today (subject) has come to find (friend.him/her). "I've been watching the huts through the storms," (subject.he/she) says. "I think I was wrong. Four turns, and cross them over. I'm sorry I told you three."

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (friend) is surprised. "You can change your mind?" "Of course I can," says (subject). "I'd be a terrible builder if I couldn't. The huts tell me what works." They go round the village together, adding a fourth turn to (friend)'s roofs. It takes all day. Neither of them minds.

o2__fx.name: Outcome B
o2__fx.text: "How do you know four is better?" asks (friend). (subject) shows (friend.him/her): the huts with three turns have rope that slipped; the ones with four don't. "I might be wrong about four, too," (subject) adds. "Ask me again next year." (friend) starts keeping (friend.his/her) own notes about rope. (friend.He/she) suspects that's what (subject) wanted all along.
